name: Judith Ellen Fan
title: Assistant Professor of Psychology, by courtesy, of Education and of Computer Science
department: Psychology (courtesy appointments in Graduate School of Education and Computer Science)
research_topics: drawing and sketching as cognitive tools
data visualization literacy and its assessment
cognitive science of learning and statistics education
cognitive-AI benchmarking / evaluating machine visual abstraction
developmental and cross-cultural studies of children's drawing
current_direction: Generative behaviors (drawing, sketching, gesture) as primary targets for cognitive models
AI in undergraduate statistics and data-science teaching at Stanford
Measuring and teaching data visualization / data literacy
Human-AI thought partnership and co-design of novel mechanisms
Cross-cultural developmental work on children's drawing and visual media
current_direction_basis: Driven by 2026 evidence: (1) Fan's single-author 2026 Current Directions in Psychological Science piece 'Generative Behaviors as Key Targets for Cognitive Models' plus the 2026 'Drawings of THINGS' dataset paper and the 2025/2026 SIGGRAPH 'Drawing & Sketching' / 'Lines and Minds' workshops she co-organized -> generative-behavior framing; (2) two Aug 6, 2026 'AI in Teaching and Learning at Stanford' grants announced on the lab news page ('Rethinking Introductory Statistics in the Age of AI' and 'Translating Instructor Expertise and Learning Science Knowledge into Individualized Course Companions') plus her Autumn teaching of PSYCH 10/STATS 60 -> AI-in-statistics-education direction; (3) the Apr 2025 Cognitive Research paper on convergence between two data visualization literacy assessments, the July 2025 'Nightingale' data & visualization literacy workshop, and the co-organized CHI 2026 'Data Literacy for the 21st Century' workshop -> data-literacy measurement thread; (4) the Mar 20, 2026 Stanford HAI seed grant 'Why didn't I think of that? Accelerating discovery of novel mechanisms by transforming human-AI co-design processes' and the Mar 2026 'Meaningful Long-Term Thought Partnerships of Minds and Machines' paper -> human-AI partnership thread; (5) 2026 OpenAlex preprints with Rebecca Zhu, Bria Long and Michael Frank on children's drawing and vocabulary in Kisumu, Kenya, plus the Dec 2025 Topics in Cognitive Science paper -> cross-cultural developmental thread. Not based on her older biography.

evidence.title: Generative Behaviors as Key Targets for Cognitive Models
evidence.summary: Single-authored theoretical piece by Fan arguing that generative behaviors should be central targets for cognitive models. Listed first on the lab papers page and retrieved from OpenAlex (publication date 2026-02-22).

evidence.title: Drawings of THINGS: A large-scale drawing dataset of 1,854 object concepts
evidence.summary: Mukherjee, Huey, Stoinski, Hebart, Fan, & Bainbridge. Large-scale drawing dataset spanning 1,854 object concepts; published version dated 2026-01-30 per OpenAlex and listed on the lab papers page.

evidence.title: Meaningful Long-Term Thought Partnerships of Minds and Machines
evidence.summary: Collins, Wong, Tenenbaum, & Fan (2026-03-30 per OpenAlex). Frames long-horizon human-AI thought partnership, matching the lab's human-AI co-design direction.

evidence.title: SketchAgent: Language-Driven Sequential Sketch Generation
evidence.summary: Vinker, Rott Shaham, Zheng, Zhao, Fan, & Torralba, CVPR 2025 (OpenAlex publication date 2025-06-10). Language-driven sequential sketch generation - the computer-vision/creative-AI side of the lab's drawing work.
evidence.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2025

evidence.title: Evaluating convergence between two data visualization literacy assessments
evidence.summary: Brockbank, Verma, Lloyd, Huey, Padilla, & Fan (2025). Administered two widely used graph comprehension assessments to N=1,113 participants and found the tests probe somewhat distinct components of data visualization literacy, motivating more comprehensive assessments.

evidence.summary: Lab news (March 10, 2026): "Judy Fan received the Lila R. Gleitman Prize for Early-Career Contributions to Cognitive Science!" Also listed under Honors & Awards on her Stanford Profiles page as "Lila R. Gleitman Prize, Cognitive Science Society (2026)".

recruiting.statement: From https://cogtoolslab.github.io/prospective.html (live text): "Dr. Fan is not currently recruiting PhD students intending to start in Fall 2027 as primary advisees, though there is some possibility of exploring co-advising arrangements with other faculty at Stanford. The lab is also not currently recruiting postdocs during AY 2026-27." The same page nevertheless keeps an open door for people already on campus: "Current Stanford students are also welcome to get involved in research in the lab, even if you are not affiliated with the Psychology department." Status is recorded as 'closed' because the only explicit recruiting declarations on the page are negative and no position is currently posted; the Stanford-student welcome is a standing invitation to make contact, not an advertised opening.

state_rationale: No live, formal, undergraduate-relevant opening exists on any page fetched. The prospective-lab-members page states "Dr. Fan is not currently recruiting PhD students intending to start in Fall 2027 as primary advisees" and "The lab is also not currently recruiting postdocs during AY 2026-27." The AY 2026-27 Lab Manager and IRiSS Predoctoral Researcher postings are present in the page source only inside HTML comments (not displayed), their stated deadlines (May 1 and May 5, 2026) have passed, and the Sept 15, 2026 news item "We welcome new IRiSS predoc fellow and Lab Manager Idil Sahin to the lab!" indicates both were filled. That rules out OPENING. But the lab is unmistakably active - two Aug 2026 Stanford AI-in-teaching grants, a Mar 2026 HAI seed grant, 2026 journal and CogSci papers, the Mar 2026 Gleitman Prize, and new 2026 lab members - and it demonstrably involves undergraduates right now (a live "Undergraduate Students" section naming David Tomz and Avery Yue, a 2026 honors thesis student, and the standing line "Current Stanford students are also welcome to get involved in research in the lab, even if you are not affiliated with the Psychology department"). A well-prepared cold email from a Stanford undergraduate is therefore reasonable, following the prospective page's instruction to read that page in full first.
